policy.frozen: Policy carried from Lab 7-8 (frozen 25 Feb 2026) and re-dated to the 23 Sep 2026 valuation date; the rules below were fixed before the multiples were computed.
rules: Business test: a listed operating company whose largest profit pool is accelerated-computing silicon sold into data centers (same customers, same capex budgets).
Earnings basis: GAAP diluted EPS and GAAP operating income, trailing twelve months to the latest 10-Q filed on or before the valuation date; no adjusted figures.
Price basis: Nasdaq close on the same trading day for every company (23 Sep 2026).
Enterprise value = market capitalisation on the cover-page share count + total debt (carrying) - cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments; no leases, no equity stakes.
A multiple above 100x is reported but marked not meaningful: at that level trailing earnings are too small relative to price to say anything about NVIDIA.
Qualified peers are used, not dropped; the qualification is stated beside the result.
No transaction (M&A) evidence: no control transaction of a comparable accelerated-computing business exists; a control premium cannot be defended for a $5tn target.

drivers.label: Revenue growth FY2028E-FY2031E, shift (pp)
drivers.unit: percentage points added to each year
drivers.bound_reason: -25 pp makes FY2028E flat (0%) and the later years shrink: the "AI capex stops" case. +25 pp is one point above the growth the market price implies (reverse DCF); nothing in the filings supports more.
drivers.challenge: Two customers are 36% of revenue (FY2026 10-K MD&A p. 41); hyperscaler capex cannot compound at 65-85% for long.
drivers.evidence: Data Center revenue growth in the next two quarterly reports; hyperscaler capex guidance.

drivers.label: FY2027E revenue vs base (Q4 judgment), %
drivers.value_note: H1 actual 177,837 + Q3 outlook 108,000 + Q4 judgment 115,000
drivers.bound_reason: Q3 is guided within +/-2%; only Q4 (14 weeks) is judgment, so +/-10% of the year is the widest a miss or beat could plausibly reach.
drivers.challenge: Q4 FY2027 has no guidance yet; export controls on China Data Center compute remain in the outlook.
drivers.evidence: Q3 FY2027 results and the Q4 outlook (expected November 2026).

drivers.label: Gross margin, shift (pp, all years)
drivers.bound_reason: -13 pp takes FY2031E to 57.0%, FY2023's 56.9% trough (the last cycle low, FY2024 10-K); +4 pp caps the first year at 78.5%, above any quarter NVIDIA has reported.
drivers.challenge: Custom silicon (Broadcom-built accelerators) and AMD compete for the same racks; CUDA lock-in is a judgment, not a filing claim.
drivers.evidence: Gross-margin guidance below 72% and falling; Data Center pricing disclosures.

drivers.label: Operating expenses / revenue, shift (pp, all years)
drivers.bound_reason: -2 pp is below the H1 FY2027 run-rate of 9.0%; +6 pp returns FY2031E to FY2024's 18.6%.
drivers.challenge: Opex grew 41% in FY2026 (compensation, compute, infrastructure); the one-year product cadence keeps R&D rising.
drivers.evidence: Opex growing faster than revenue for two consecutive quarters.

drivers.label: Tax rate (all years)
drivers.value_note: Q2 FY2027 release: FY2027 GAAP rate 16-18%
drivers.bound_reason: FY2024 was 12.0%; 21% is the statutory rate with no FDDEI, SBC or R&D benefit.
drivers.challenge: FDDEI and SBC benefits shrink as the mix changes; the rate rose each of the last three years.
drivers.evidence: Effective rate in the next 10-K; tax-law changes.

drivers.label: Capital spending / revenue
drivers.bound_reason: FY2024 1.8% is the low; 6% is double the FY2026 ratio, the most a fabless company has needed.
drivers.challenge: MD&A says capex will increase in FY2027; a ratio on 86% revenue growth already delivers 11.2bn.
drivers.evidence: Purchases of property and equipment in the cash flow statement; any move to own fabs.

drivers.label: Stock-based compensation / revenue
drivers.bound_reason: H1 FY2027 2.2% is the low; FY2024 5.8% is the high of the three filed years.
drivers.challenge: SBC is added back as non-cash; treat it as a cash cost (toggle) and value falls.
drivers.evidence: SBC line in the cash flow statement; share count after buybacks.

drivers.label: Cost of equity
drivers.value_note: judgment between the tutorial 10% and the measured CAPM 13-14.8%
drivers.bound_reason: 9% is a beta of about 0.9 (below the market); 16% is the observed beta 2.21 plus one standard error (2.5) at rf 5% + ERP 4.42%.
drivers.challenge: beta.py measures 2.21 raw (s.e. 0.30), 1.81 Blume; CAPM gives 13.0-14.8%, so 12% is the generous end.
drivers.evidence: Re-estimated beta each quarter; the ten-year Treasury yield.

drivers.label: Terminal growth after FY2031E
drivers.bound_reason: 0% is a flat industry after the build-out; 4% is about nominal GDP, the most a going concern can hold forever.
drivers.challenge: In FY2031E the model reinvests 2.5% of net income and grows 3% forever, a 118% return on retained cash.
drivers.evidence: Terminal growth must stay below the discount rate; the check refuses otherwise.

method_disagreement: FCFF DCF (base $124; causal range $80-$187) values the cash flows the filings and guidance support; it assumes growth decelerates from 25% to 4% after FY2027 and a 12% cost of equity.
The FCFE cross-check from Lab 10 gives $123.05: the two cash-flow definitions agree within a dollar because NVIDIA carries almost no net debt.

Trailing GAAP multiples disagree with the DCF in both directions. NVIDIA itself trades at 28.5x trailing earnings and 27.4x trailing EBIT; Broadcom at 45.3x and 40.4x, which applied to NVIDIA's trailing figures implies $358 (P/E) and $332 (EV/EBIT). AMD's 158x P/E and 153x EV/EBIT are reported but not meaningful: its 16% operating margin against NVIDIA's 65% means the market is capitalising a recovery, not current earnings.

Why they disagree: a trailing multiple capitalises last year's earnings at whatever growth the market expects of the peer; the DCF capitalises my explicit growth path. The peer multiples say the market expects NVIDIA's earnings to keep compounding well past FY2028; the DCF says the filings do not yet show that. The methods are not averaged: the DCF is the supported value, the multiples describe what the price is paying for.

Reverse DCF puts the disagreement in operating language: the price needs about +24 pp more growth in each of FY2028-FY2031 (a path near 49%, 36%, 31%, 28%), or a cost of equity near 8.0%, or terminal growth near 7.8%; no gross-margin or opex assumption inside the defended bounds reaches it.
